short: Frame-wise ultrasound CNN VAD (M06) and audio-VAD labels (M02) are standard; one-speaker file-split test (M12) is behind held-out-speaker VAD work; 85% is 11 points over majority.
position: The paper [@shandiz2021vad] changes two components: a single-frame 2D CNN labelling ultrasound tongue frames as speech or silence (M06), trained on acoustic-VAD labels from the parallel audio (M02). Both are standard: a single-frame CNN VAD on lip images with audio-derived labels dates from 2015 [@cornu2015voicing], and an ultrasound tongue-activity speech detector from 2019 [@ribeiro2019ultrasound]; the paper discusses only acoustic VAD (Sec. 3). The evaluation (M12) is behind the best comparable work: four checked earlier non-acoustic VAD studies (of 46 pattern matches, Appendix) tested held-out speakers, the best reaching 92.2% on unseen GRID speakers with lip video [@sharma2019visual]; this paper tests one speaker on a file split, holding out no TaL1 session. Accuracy 0.852 is about 11 points above always answering "speech", and 43% of silence frames are kept (inference, Table 6). The claim that ultrasound VAD "performed similarly" to speech VAD (Sec. 5.4) rests on MCD changes of 0.01 to 0.05 and MSE changes of mixed sign, with no repeated runs or test.
